name: 原位 DRIFTS 断轴/整轴时间序列堆叠 (In Situ DRIFTS Stack)
when: In situ DRIFTS time-series (e.g. 12 spectra: 1-60 min + N2 purge) or catalyst comparison stacks across reverse wavenumber axes, optionally with a broken x-axis omitting the silent C-H/CO2 window (3300-1800 cm^-1).

required_slots.series: Time-ordered or sample-ordered absorbance / Kubelka-Munk columns (typically 12 curves: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60 min + N2 purge 60 min, or 3 catalysts).

optional_slots.segments: Broken x-axis segments [[3800, 3300, w1], [1800, 800, w2]] with break_gap; omit for unbroken panels like FigS10 (1800-1200 cm^-1)!
optional_slots.vlines: Vertical dashed peak markers scoped to specific segment index (`seg: 0` or `seg: 1`) with non-overlapping wavenumber labels.
optional_slots.inline_time_labels: Right-side in-frame time labels (1 min .. 60 min, N2 purge 60 min) positioned cleanly above each curve tail.

data_contract.y_meaning: Absorbance (a.u.) or Kubelka-Munk (a.u.) with numeric y-ticks suppressed.
constraints: CRITICAL: Check whether each figure uses broken axis or unbroken axis! Fig6, FigS9, FigS11, FigS12 use broken axis (3800-3300 & 1800-800); FigS10 is UNBROKEN 1800-1200 cm^-1!
Summary Excel files in data/drifts/ use union of x-grids across CSVs -> boundary cells can be NaN; enable dropna: true per curve.
Apply transparent ops (baseline_min / baseline_linear / savgol / explicit scale & offset) so curves are crisp and NOT flat, and log every op to .provenance.json.
NEVER normalize curves individually — preserve relative band growth/decay over time.

notes: Wide 1x3 figures (FigS9 7.09x2.12 in, FigS10 7.09x2.08 in) use smaller PDF-matched sizes: labels ~9.9pt, ticks ~7.1pt, annotations ~4.9pt, frame 1.08pt, curves 0.56pt.
1x2 figures (FigS11, FigS12 at 7.09x3.01 in) & 2x2 Fig6 (7.09x6.02 in) use standard 14.1/10.2/7.1pt, frame 1.55pt, curves 0.80pt.
Author OMNIC smoothing/baseline settings are not stored in the package; any savgol/baseline op used in reproduction must be explicitly documented in spec.ops and provenance.
